note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_iterable v1.6.0 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. STRING_AGG/ARRAY_AGG without ORDER BY given ORDER BY its own argument (ASC NULLS FIRST) so the output does not depend on row order (these tables, and tables reading them, are checked against the duckdb compiled SQL with the same change rather than dbt's table): int_iterable__campaign_labels, iterable__users. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 67 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: iterable__list_user_history 17). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_iterable__list_tmp -> list_data; stg_iterable__list_user_tmp -> list_user_data; stg_iterable__user_history_tmp -> user_history_data.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_iterable v1.6.0 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. STRING_AGG/ARRAY_AGG without ORDER BY given ORDER BY its own argument (ASC NULLS FIRST) so the output does not depend on row order (these tables, and tables reading them, are checked against the duckdb compiled SQL with the same change rather than dbt's table): int_iterable__campaign_labels, iterable__users. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 67 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: iterable__user_campaign 5). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_iterable__campaign_history_tmp -> campaign_history_data; stg_iterable__channel_tmp -> channel_data; stg_iterable__event_extension_tmp -> event_extension_data; stg_iterable__event_tmp -> event_data; stg_iterable__message_type_tmp -> message_type_data; stg_iterable__template_history_tmp -> template_history_data; stg_iterable__user_history_tmp -> user_history_data.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_iterable v1.6.0 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. STRING_AGG/ARRAY_AGG without ORDER BY given ORDER BY its own argument (ASC NULLS FIRST) so the output does not depend on row order (these tables, and tables reading them, are checked against the duckdb compiled SQL with the same change rather than dbt's table): int_iterable__campaign_labels, iterable__users. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 67 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: iterable__user_unsubscriptions 0). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_iterable__channel_tmp -> channel_data; stg_iterable__message_type_tmp -> message_type_data; stg_iterable__user_unsub_message_type_tmp -> user_unsubscribed_message_type_data; stg_iterable__user_unsubscribed_channel_tmp -> user_unsubscribed_channel_data.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_iterable v1.6.0 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. STRING_AGG/ARRAY_AGG without ORDER BY given ORDER BY its own argument (ASC NULLS FIRST) so the output does not depend on row order (these tables, and tables reading them, are checked against the duckdb compiled SQL with the same change rather than dbt's table): int_iterable__campaign_labels, iterable__users. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 67 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: iterable__users 13). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_iterable__campaign_history_tmp -> campaign_history_data; stg_iterable__channel_tmp -> channel_data; stg_iterable__event_extension_tmp -> event_extension_data; stg_iterable__event_tmp -> event_data; stg_iterable__list_user_tmp -> list_user_data; stg_iterable__message_type_tmp -> message_type_data; stg_iterable__template_history_tmp -> template_history_data; stg_iterable__user_history_tmp -> user_history_data.

Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 50 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: klaviyo__campaigns 0). Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 50 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: klaviyo__events 0). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_klaviyo__campaign_tmp -> campaign; stg_klaviyo__event_tmp -> event; stg_klaviyo__flow_tmp -> flow; stg_klaviyo__metric_tmp -> metric; stg_klaviyo__person_tmp -> person.

Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_mailchimp v1.3.2 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_mailchimp v1.3.2 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 50 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: mailchimp__automation_activities 0). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_mailchimp__automation_activities_tmp -> automation_recipient_activity; stg_mailchimp__automation_emails_tmp -> automation_email; stg_mailchimp__automations_tmp -> automation.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_mailchimp v1.3.2 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 50 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: mailchimp__automation_emails 0). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_mailchimp__automation_activities_tmp -> automation_recipient_activity; stg_mailchimp__automation_emails_tmp -> automation_email; stg_mailchimp__automation_recipients_tmp -> automation_recipient; stg_mailchimp__automations_tmp -> automation; stg_mailchimp__unsubscribes_tmp -> unsubscribe.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_mailchimp v1.3.2 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 50 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: mailchimp__automations 0). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_mailchimp__automation_activities_tmp -> automation_recipient_activity; stg_mailchimp__automation_emails_tmp -> automation_email; stg_mailchimp__automation_recipients_tmp -> automation_recipient; stg_mailchimp__automations_tmp -> automation; stg_mailchimp__unsubscribes_tmp -> unsubscribe.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_mailchimp v1.3.2 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 50 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: mailchimp__campaign_activities 0). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_mailchimp__campaign_activities_tmp -> campaign_recipient_activity; stg_mailchimp__campaigns_tmp -> campaign.

Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 50 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: mailchimp__campaign_recipients 0). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_mailchimp__campaign_activities_tmp -> campaign_recipient_activity; stg_mailchimp__campaign_recipients_tmp -> campaign_recipient; stg_mailchimp__campaigns_tmp -> campaign; stg_mailchimp__unsubscribes_tmp -> unsubscribe.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_mailchimp v1.3.2 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 50 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: mailchimp__campaigns 0). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_mailchimp__campaign_activities_tmp -> campaign_recipient_activity; stg_mailchimp__campaign_recipients_tmp -> campaign_recipient; stg_mailchimp__campaigns_tmp -> campaign; stg_mailchimp__unsubscribes_tmp -> unsubscribe.

Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 50 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: mailchimp__lists 0). note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_mailchimp v1.3.2 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 50 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: mailchimp__members 0). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_mailchimp__automation_activities_tmp -> automation_recipient_activity; stg_mailchimp__automation_emails_tmp -> automation_email; stg_mailchimp__automation_recipients_tmp -> automation_recipient; stg_mailchimp__automations_tmp -> automation; stg_mailchimp__campaign_activities_tmp -> campaign_recipient_activity; stg_mailchimp__campaign_recipients_tmp -> campaign_recipient; stg_mailchimp__campaigns_tmp -> campaign; stg_mailchimp__members_tmp -> member; stg_mailchimp__unsubscribes_tmp -> unsubscribe.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_mailchimp v1.3.2 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 50 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: mailchimp__segments 0). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_mailchimp__automation_activities_tmp -> automation_recipient_activity; stg_mailchimp__automation_emails_tmp -> automation_email; stg_mailchimp__automation_recipients_tmp -> automation_recipient; stg_mailchimp__automations_tmp -> automation; stg_mailchimp__campaign_activities_tmp -> campaign_recipient_activity; stg_mailchimp__campaign_recipients_tmp -> campaign_recipient; stg_mailchimp__campaigns_tmp -> campaign; stg_mailchimp__lists_tmp -> list; stg_mailchimp__segments_tmp -> segment; stg_mailchimp__unsubscribes_tmp -> unsubscribe.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_recurly v1.5.1 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. now()/current_timestamp replaced by TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' and current_date by DATE '2026-01-01' in: int_recurly__account_cumulatives, recurly__account_overview. Matched dbt's table only at 6 significant digits (float32 seed columns read as FLOAT64): stg_recurly__line_item_history_tmp, stg_recurly__subscription_history, stg_recurly__account_balance_history_tmp, stg_recurly__credit_payment_history_tmp, stg_recurly__plan_currency_history. 10 models dropped (failed the round trip or downstream of one): int_recurly__account_cumulatives, int_recurly__account_partitions, int_recurly__account_rolling_totals, int_recurly__account_running_totals, int_recurly__transactions_date_spine, int_recurly__transactions_grouped, recurly__account_daily_overview, recurly__account_overview, recurly__churn_analysis, recurly__subscription_overview. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 62 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: recurly__balance_transactions 12, recurly__line_item_enhanced 11, recurly__monthly_recurring_revenue 5). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_recurly__account_history_tmp -> account_history_data; stg_recurly__invoice_history_tmp -> invoice_history_data; stg_recurly__line_item_history_tmp -> line_item_history_data; stg_recurly__plan_history_tmp -> plan_history_data; stg_recurly__subscription_history_tmp -> subscription_history_data; stg_recurly__transaction_tmp -> transaction_data.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_recurly v1.5.1 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. now()/current_timestamp replaced by TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' and current_date by DATE '2026-01-01' in: int_recurly__account_cumulatives, recurly__account_overview. Matched dbt's table only at 6 significant digits (float32 seed columns read as FLOAT64): stg_recurly__line_item_history_tmp, stg_recurly__subscription_history, stg_recurly__account_balance_history_tmp, stg_recurly__credit_payment_history_tmp, stg_recurly__plan_currency_history. 10 models dropped (failed the round trip or downstream of one): int_recurly__account_cumulatives, int_recurly__account_partitions, int_recurly__account_rolling_totals, int_recurly__account_running_totals, int_recurly__transactions_date_spine, int_recurly__transactions_grouped, recurly__account_daily_overview, recurly__account_overview, recurly__churn_analysis, recurly__subscription_overview. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 62 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: recurly__balance_transactions 12). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_recurly__invoice_history_tmp -> invoice_history_data; stg_recurly__line_item_history_tmp -> line_item_history_data; stg_recurly__transaction_tmp -> transaction_data.

Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. now()/current_timestamp replaced by TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' and current_date by DATE '2026-01-01' in: int_recurly__account_cumulatives, recurly__account_overview. Matched dbt's table only at 6 significant digits (float32 seed columns read as FLOAT64): stg_recurly__line_item_history_tmp, stg_recurly__subscription_history, stg_recurly__account_balance_history_tmp, stg_recurly__credit_payment_history_tmp, stg_recurly__plan_currency_history. 10 models dropped (failed the round trip or downstream of one): int_recurly__account_cumulatives, int_recurly__account_partitions, int_recurly__account_rolling_totals, int_recurly__account_running_totals, int_recurly__transactions_date_spine, int_recurly__transactions_grouped, recurly__account_daily_overview, recurly__account_overview, recurly__churn_analysis, recurly__subscription_overview. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 62 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: recurly__line_item_enhanced 11). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_recurly__account_history_tmp -> account_history_data; stg_recurly__invoice_history_tmp -> invoice_history_data; stg_recurly__line_item_history_tmp -> line_item_history_data; stg_recurly__plan_history_tmp -> plan_history_data; stg_recurly__subscription_history_tmp -> subscription_history_data; stg_recurly__transaction_tmp -> transaction_data.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_recurly v1.5.1 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. now()/current_timestamp replaced by TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' and current_date by DATE '2026-01-01' in: int_recurly__account_cumulatives, recurly__account_overview. Matched dbt's table only at 6 significant digits (float32 seed columns read as FLOAT64): stg_recurly__line_item_history_tmp, stg_recurly__subscription_history, stg_recurly__account_balance_history_tmp, stg_recurly__credit_payment_history_tmp, stg_recurly__plan_currency_history. 10 models dropped (failed the round trip or downstream of one): int_recurly__account_cumulatives, int_recurly__account_partitions, int_recurly__account_rolling_totals, int_recurly__account_running_totals, int_recurly__transactions_date_spine, int_recurly__transactions_grouped, recurly__account_daily_overview, recurly__account_overview, recurly__churn_analysis, recurly__subscription_overview. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 62 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: recurly__monthly_recurring_revenue 5). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_recurly__account_history_tmp -> account_history_data; stg_recurly__invoice_history_tmp -> invoice_history_data; stg_recurly__line_item_history_tmp -> line_item_history_data; stg_recurly__transaction_tmp -> transaction_data.

Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. now()/current_timestamp replaced by TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' and current_date by DATE '2026-01-01' in: int_github__issue_open_length, int_github__pull_request_times. STRING_AGG/ARRAY_AGG without ORDER BY given ORDER BY its own argument (ASC NULLS FIRST) so the output does not depend on row order (these tables, and tables reading them, are checked against the duckdb compiled SQL with the same change rather than dbt's table): int_github__issue_assignees, int_github__issue_labels, int_github__pull_request_reviewers, int_github__repository_teams. 1 models dropped (failed the round trip or downstream of one): github__weekly_metrics. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 51 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: github__daily_metrics 1, github__issues 1, github__monthly_metrics 1, github__pull_requests 0, github__quarterly_metrics 1). Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. now()/current_timestamp replaced by TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' and current_date by DATE '2026-01-01' in: int_github__issue_open_length, int_github__pull_request_times. STRING_AGG/ARRAY_AGG without ORDER BY given ORDER BY its own argument (ASC NULLS FIRST) so the output does not depend on row order (these tables, and tables reading them, are checked against the duckdb compiled SQL with the same change rather than dbt's table): int_github__issue_assignees, int_github__issue_labels, int_github__pull_request_reviewers, int_github__repository_teams. 1 models dropped (failed the round trip or downstream of one): github__weekly_metrics. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 51 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: github__daily_metrics 1). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_github__issue_assignee_tmp -> github_issue_assignee_data; stg_github__issue_closed_history_tmp -> github_issue_closed_history_data; stg_github__issue_comment_tmp -> github_issue_comment_data; stg_github__issue_label_tmp -> github_issue_label_data; stg_github__issue_merged_tmp -> github_issue_merged_data; stg_github__issue_tmp -> github_issue_data; stg_github__label_tmp -> github_label_data; stg_github__pull_request_review_tmp -> github_pull_request_review_data; stg_github__pull_request_tmp -> github_pull_request_data; stg_github__repo_team_tmp -> github_repo_team_data; stg_github__repository_tmp -> github_repository_data; stg_github__requested_reviewer_history_tmp -> github_requested_reviewer_history_data; stg_github__team_tmp -> github_team_data; stg_github__user_tmp -> github_user_data.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_github v1.4.1 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. now()/current_timestamp replaced by TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' and current_date by DATE '2026-01-01' in: int_github__issue_open_length, int_github__pull_request_times. STRING_AGG/ARRAY_AGG without ORDER BY given ORDER BY its own argument (ASC NULLS FIRST) so the output does not depend on row order (these tables, and tables reading them, are checked against the duckdb compiled SQL with the same change rather than dbt's table): int_github__issue_assignees, int_github__issue_labels, int_github__pull_request_reviewers, int_github__repository_teams. 1 models dropped (failed the round trip or downstream of one): github__weekly_metrics. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 51 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: github__issues 1). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_github__issue_assignee_tmp -> github_issue_assignee_data; stg_github__issue_closed_history_tmp -> github_issue_closed_history_data; stg_github__issue_comment_tmp -> github_issue_comment_data; stg_github__issue_label_tmp -> github_issue_label_data; stg_github__issue_merged_tmp -> github_issue_merged_data; stg_github__issue_tmp -> github_issue_data; stg_github__label_tmp -> github_label_data; stg_github__pull_request_review_tmp -> github_pull_request_review_data; stg_github__pull_request_tmp -> github_pull_request_data; stg_github__repo_team_tmp -> github_repo_team_data; stg_github__repository_tmp -> github_repository_data; stg_github__requested_reviewer_history_tmp -> github_requested_reviewer_history_data; stg_github__team_tmp -> github_team_data; stg_github__user_tmp -> github_user_data.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_github v1.4.1 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. now()/current_timestamp replaced by TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' and current_date by DATE '2026-01-01' in: int_github__issue_open_length, int_github__pull_request_times. STRING_AGG/ARRAY_AGG without ORDER BY given ORDER BY its own argument (ASC NULLS FIRST) so the output does not depend on row order (these tables, and tables reading them, are checked against the duckdb compiled SQL with the same change rather than dbt's table): int_github__issue_assignees, int_github__issue_labels, int_github__pull_request_reviewers, int_github__repository_teams. 1 models dropped (failed the round trip or downstream of one): github__weekly_metrics. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 51 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: github__monthly_metrics 1). note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_github v1.4.1 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. now()/current_timestamp replaced by TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' and current_date by DATE '2026-01-01' in: int_github__issue_open_length, int_github__pull_request_times. STRING_AGG/ARRAY_AGG without ORDER BY given ORDER BY its own argument (ASC NULLS FIRST) so the output does not depend on row order (these tables, and tables reading them, are checked against the duckdb compiled SQL with the same change rather than dbt's table): int_github__issue_assignees, int_github__issue_labels, int_github__pull_request_reviewers, int_github__repository_teams. 1 models dropped (failed the round trip or downstream of one): github__weekly_metrics. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 51 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: github__pull_requests 0). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_github__issue_assignee_tmp -> github_issue_assignee_data; stg_github__issue_closed_history_tmp -> github_issue_closed_history_data; stg_github__issue_comment_tmp -> github_issue_comment_data; stg_github__issue_label_tmp -> github_issue_label_data; stg_github__issue_merged_tmp -> github_issue_merged_data; stg_github__issue_tmp -> github_issue_data; stg_github__label_tmp -> github_label_data; stg_github__pull_request_review_tmp -> github_pull_request_review_data; stg_github__pull_request_tmp -> github_pull_request_data; stg_github__repo_team_tmp -> github_repo_team_data; stg_github__repository_tmp -> github_repository_data; stg_github__requested_reviewer_history_tmp -> github_requested_reviewer_history_data; stg_github__team_tmp -> github_team_data; stg_github__user_tmp -> github_user_data.

note: Adapted from fivetran/dbt_github v1.4.1 integration_tests, built with dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-duckdb 1.11 (fivetran_utils v0.4.13, dbt_utils 1.3.0) with every package model forced to materialized=table (ephemeral/view/incremental -> table) and the source schema vars set to the seed schema. Compiled DuckDB SQL: relation names made bare (models by name, sources by seed table name), comments dropped, transpiled duckdb -> bigquery with sqlglot 30.21.0; each table transpiled back to duckdb reproduces dbt's rows on the seed data (time-dependent tables: reproduces the duckdb compiled SQL with the same fixed time). Sources are the project's seeds; seed types mapped INTEGER/BIGINT->INT64, VARCHAR->STRING, FLOAT/DOUBLE->FLOAT64 (FLOAT seeds rounded to 7 significant digits), DECIMAL->NUMERIC. No keys declared. now()/current_timestamp replaced by TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' and current_date by DATE '2026-01-01' in: int_github__issue_open_length, int_github__pull_request_times. STRING_AGG/ARRAY_AGG without ORDER BY given ORDER BY its own argument (ASC NULLS FIRST) so the output does not depend on row order (these tables, and tables reading them, are checked against the duckdb compiled SQL with the same change rather than dbt's table): int_github__issue_assignees, int_github__issue_labels, int_github__pull_request_reviewers, int_github__repository_teams. 1 models dropped (failed the round trip or downstream of one): github__weekly_metrics. Reference (dead tables and pass-through tables removed): verified equal on the seed database and 51 random databases (DuckDB, optimizer off, bags with column names in order, floats compared at 12 significant digits); a random database counts for a protected table only when the original gives the same output with every source's rows reversed (order-sensitive outputs skipped: github__quarterly_metrics 1). Pass-through tables replaced by what they read: stg_github__issue_assignee_tmp -> github_issue_assignee_data; stg_github__issue_closed_history_tmp -> github_issue_closed_history_data; stg_github__issue_comment_tmp -> github_issue_comment_data; stg_github__issue_label_tmp -> github_issue_label_data; stg_github__issue_merged_tmp -> github_issue_merged_data; stg_github__issue_tmp -> github_issue_data; stg_github__label_tmp -> github_label_data; stg_github__pull_request_review_tmp -> github_pull_request_review_data; stg_github__pull_request_tmp -> github_pull_request_data; stg_github__repo_team_tmp -> github_repo_team_data; stg_github__repository_tmp -> github_repository_data; stg_github__requested_reviewer_history_tmp -> github_requested_reviewer_history_data; stg_github__team_tmp -> github_team_data; stg_github__user_tmp -> github_user_data.
